1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status current with `--status` and its strategy prose current with
60	  `--summary` / `--summary-file` (there is no `--strategy` flag). It doubles as
61	  the **project board**:
62	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
63	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
64	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
65	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
66	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
67	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
68	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
69	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
70	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
71	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
72	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
73	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
74	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
75	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
76	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
77	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
78	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
79	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
80	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
81	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
82	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
83	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
84	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
85	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
86	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
87	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
88	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
89	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
90	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
91	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
92	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
93	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
94	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
95	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
96	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
97	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
98	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
99	
100	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
101	
102	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
103	
104	| Variable | Meaning |
105	|---|---|
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
112	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
113	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
114	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
115	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
116	
117	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
118	
119	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
120	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
121	
122	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
123	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
124	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
125	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
126	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
127	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
128	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
129	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
130	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
131	
132	## One-shot discipline (important)
133	
134	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
135	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
136	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
137	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
138	
139	## Pick the highest-value work
140	
141	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
142	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
143	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
144	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
145	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
146	
147	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
148	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
149	the objective is large. Leave a `"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body …`
150	at each significant step. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
151	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
152	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
153	(it returns to the queue).
154	
155	## Fresh-context checkpoints
156	
157	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
158	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
159	checkpoints:
160	
161	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
162	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
163	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
164	  clean/build result.
165	
166	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
167	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
168	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
169	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
170	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
171	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
172	terminal `done` claim.
173	
174	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
175	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
176	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
177	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
178	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
179	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
180	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
181	
182	## Warnings are work
183	
184	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
185	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
186	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
187	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
188	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
189	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
190	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
191	why.
192	
193	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
194	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
195	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
196	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
197	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
198	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
199	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
200	
201	## Do the work (Lean)
202	
203	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
204	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
205	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
206	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
207	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
208	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
209	configured final build covers the same files.
210	
211	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
212	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
213	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
214	mathlib — query it:
215	
216	| You want | Use | Not |
217	|---|---|---|
218	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
219	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
220	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
221	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
222	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
223	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
224	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
225	
226	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
227	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
228	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
229	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
230	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
231	back to grep.
232	
233	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
234	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
235	
236	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
237	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
238	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
239	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
240	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
241	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
242	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
243	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
244	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
245	
246	## Read the other projects
247	
248	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
249	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
250	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
251	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
252	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
253	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
254	
255	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
256	
257	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
258	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
259	needs no permission.
260	
261	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
262	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
263	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
264	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
265	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
266	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
267	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
268	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
269	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
270	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
271	
272	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
273	
274	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
275	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
276	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
277	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
278	
279	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
280	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
281	
282	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status (`--status`) and strategy prose
283	  (`--summary`), not a re-narration of the diff.
284	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
285	  as **memory**.
286	
287	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
288	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
289	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
290	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
291	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
292	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
293	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
294	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
295	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
296	
297	## Resuming after an interruption
298	
299	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
300	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
301	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
302	
303	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
304	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
305	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
306	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
307	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
308	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
309	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
310	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
311	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
312	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
313	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
314	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
315	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
316	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
317	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
318	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
319	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
320	
321	## Final report (your last message)
322	
323	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
324	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
325	Recommended sections: `## Summary`, `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
326	`## Why I stopped`, `## Next` (keep at least `## Progress` and
327	`## Why I stopped`). In `## Progress`, one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
328	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
329	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
330	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
331	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
332	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is

5	
6	Your prompt carries the task and nothing else: no history, no word about who ran
7	before you or how they ended. That is deliberate — state is pulled, not pushed
8	(the `horizon` skill's stance). But it means a session that starts working
9	immediately is guessing. Usually somebody *was* here before you, often minutes
10	ago, and their report was written for you.
11	
12	This skill is the first pass: four cheap reads, a guess at the situation, then
13	the context that situation actually calls for. Budget a couple of minutes, not a
14	tenth of the session.
15	
16	## The four signals
17	
18	```bash
19	ls "$ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR/.."     # sibling sessions in THIS run
20	"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json             # `paused` (why the last run stopped) + `recent_failure_reasons`
21	"$HORIZON_BIN" ps                       # is another run live on this workspace RIGHT NOW?
22	"$HORIZON_GIT" log --oneline -15        # what actually landed recently
23	```
24	
25	The sibling listing is the one that decides most of it. A run's sessions look
26	like:
27	
28	```
29	0001-system            ← orchestrator bookkeeping (commits, integration), not an agent
30	0002-horizon-PET.5     ← a horizon session; meta.json + transcript.jsonl + usage.json
31	0003-system
32	0004-horizon-PET.5     ← ...you, probably
33	```
34	
35	For any earlier `*-horizon-*` sibling, two files answer everything:
36	
37	- **`report.md` present** → that session finished on its own terms and wrote you
38	  a hand-off. **`report.md` absent** → it was killed mid-flight. This is the
39	  single most informative bit on disk.
40	- **`meta.json`** → `round`, `task_id`, `status`, `started_at`, `ended_at`,
41	  `model`. `ended_at` against the current time tells you whether "recent" means
42	  four minutes ago or last week.
43	
44	## Which situation am I in?
45	
46	Work down the list; the first match is your best guess.
47	
48	**An earlier horizon sibling has no `report.md`** → *resume after a crash or
49	kill.* Its work is half-done and possibly half-committed. Read its commits in
50	the ledger first (they are the part that survived), then the tail of its
51	transcript to see what it was in the middle of — `usage --json` `paused` gives
52	the reason it died (usage limit, budget, auth), and `recent_failure_reasons`
53	shows rate-limit pressure that may still be there. Trust the ledger over the
54	transcript: anything it did not commit is gone, no matter what it said it was
55	doing. If the dead session shares your `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK`, you are continuing
56	its exact work — pick up its front rather than opening a new one.
57	
58	**An earlier horizon sibling has a `report.md`** → *hand-off from the session
59	that just finished.* The common case. Read that report first — its `## Next` and
60	`## Why I stopped` were written for exactly this moment — then its commits, then
61	any inbox items addressed to horizon since its `ended_at`. Do not re-derive what
62	it already established; do not redo a piece it says is done without checking the
63	ledger.
64	
65	**`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is `0` and no horizon sibling exists** → *first agent
66	of the run.* Nobody handed you anything **in this run** — but the workspace is
67	almost never greenfield. Earlier runs live under `.archon-horizon/runs/`; the
68	roadmap, the inbox and the ledger carry their conclusions. Skim the roadmap and
69	recent ledger history before deciding a strategy that a previous run already
70	tried and rejected.

72	**`ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` is unset** → *not launched by the orchestrator* (an
73	interactive or hand-driven session). No run context exists to reconstruct;
74	orient from workspace state — roadmap, inbox, ledger — and say where things
75	stand before proposing work.

78	for "am I first" — but a resumed run can re-run a round whose session died, so a
79	`0` with a dead sibling present means *resume*, not *fresh*. The dead-sibling
80	check settles it either way. (`ROUND + 1 == ROUNDS` is a sound last-round test,
81	resumed runs included — `ROUNDS` bounds the rounds *this* invocation drives, not
82	the run's original plan.)

86	- **`horizon ps` said another run is live?** You share one ledger branch with it.
87	  Commit in small coherent pieces and expect to see its commits interleaved.
88	- **Timestamps are context.** A predecessor that ended 90 seconds ago probably
89	  left a warm build; one that ended last week may have left a workspace that no
90	  longer compiles. Check rather than assume.

92	  horizon, and the task's own comments if you share their `task_id`
93	  (`"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`). Skill:

2	
3	Adopted after the 2026-07-16 evening wave's four incidents (I-0149). These rules extend the
4	standing handoff protocol (07-14/14b/15) for any session running two or more lanes in this
5	workspace.
6	
7	## 1. Ledger commits: private index + compare-and-swap (the shared-index race)
8	
9	All lanes commit through one `workspace.git`; concurrent `git add`+`commit` through the
10	SHARED index can interleave and record spurious deletions of another lane's
11	freshly-committed files (happened in `6197c9676`, 862 lines vanished from HEAD, restored
12	byte-identical in `a640fef5b`). Concurrent lanes MUST commit via a private index:
13	
14	```bash
15	cd /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
16	GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git
17	export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
18	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. read-tree HEAD
19	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. add <ONLY your paths…>
20	TREE=$(git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. write-tree)
21	PARENT=$(git --git-dir=$GD rev-parse HEAD)
22	COMMIT=$(git --git-dir=$GD -c user.name="Archon Horizon" -c user.email="archon-horizon@local" \
23	  commit-tree $TREE -p $PARENT -m "<math-first message>
24	
25	Archon-Commit: agent
26	Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>")
27	git --git-dir=$GD update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT $PARENT   # CAS: fails if HEAD moved
28	unset GIT_INDEX_FILE
29	```
30	
31	If the `update-ref` CAS fails (HEAD moved), re-read HEAD and repeat — never force.
32	ALWAYS verify afterward: `git --git-dir=$GD show --stat HEAD` must touch only your paths.
33	A single-lane session may keep the plain `add`+`commit` recipe, but must still verify.
34	
35	### 1a. THE RECIPE ABOVE HAS A RACE — read HEAD ONCE, not twice (2026-07-28, run 0072)
36	
37	**As written, the recipe reads `HEAD` twice**: once in `read-tree HEAD`, and again several lines
38	later in `PARENT=$(… rev-parse HEAD)`. If another lane's CAS lands **between those two reads**,
39	your tree is built from the *old* snapshot while your parent is the *new* commit — and
40	`update-ref` **succeeds**, because it only checks that the ref has not moved since `rev-parse`.
41	It never checks that the tree was built from that ref. You publish a stale tree, silently
42	reverting everything that landed in the window.
43	
44	**Measured once, and the measurement is narrow — do not over-read it.** `e964967e8` has parent
45	`a1ef4d59c` and, diffed against *that parent*, deletes 95 lines of
46	`informal/w4-rep-critical-path.md`, 52 of `informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md` and 19 of

48	Its `read-tree` ran before `a1ef4d59c` landed; its parent was captured after. It staged explicit
49	paths and the pathspec *was* honoured: **the sweep came from the TREE BASE, not the pathspec**,
50	which is why "stage explicit files" is not a defence and why the symptom is indistinguishable
51	from §1b's shared-index staleness.
52	
53	**Two other lanes audited their own CAS commits the same day (fifteen commits between them,
54	recipe verbatim) and found zero reverts.** That is consistent with this: the race only fires when
55	another lane's CAS lands inside your particular window, so clean commits are the expected
56	outcome, not evidence of absence. The discriminating question is not "did my commits look clean"
57	but "was my `read-tree` separated from my `rev-parse` by somebody else's commit". Treat §1a as
58	cheap insurance, not as a diagnosis of every mystery revert — and check §1b too.

60	**The fix is one line — capture the parent BEFORE the tree, and read-tree that sha:**
61	
62	```bash
63	PARENT=$(git --git-dir=$GD rev-parse HEAD)     # ONCE, up front
64	export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
65	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. read-tree $PARENT      # not "HEAD"
66	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. add <ONLY your paths…>
67	TREE=$(git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. write-tree)
68	COMMIT=$(git --git-dir=$GD … commit-tree $TREE -p $PARENT -m "…")
69	git --git-dir=$GD update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT $PARENT   # now genuinely atomic
70	```
71	
72	Then a mid-recipe CAS by another lane makes `update-ref` **fail**, you re-read and retry, and the

105	
106	`/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock` is acquired by `mkdir` (atomic; a crash leaves a
107	directory that the next holder's timeout logic can reap). It is NOT a flock file: a lane
108	that runs `flock /tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock …` creates a plain FILE at the
109	path, and every mkdir-acquire loop then spins forever (this deadlocked all lanes
110	15:18–19:10 on 2026-07-16 until a human deleted it). Acquire pattern:
111	
112	```bash
113	LOCK=/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock
114	while ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; do
115	  # (a) plain FILE at the path = a flock protocol-violation; reap immediately.
116	  if [ -f "$LOCK" ]; then echo "STALE: plain file at $LOCK (flock violation) — removing" >&2; rm -f "$LOCK"; continue; fi
117	  # (b) orphaned DIRECTORY from a crashed build (rmdir never ran). Reap on proof of death:
118	  if [ -d "$LOCK" ]; then
119	    holder=$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)
120	    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
121	      echo "STALE: holder pid $holder dead — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
122	    fi
123	    # No pidfile (old-cohort holder): reap only if NO live lake build AND the dir is >15 min old.
124	    if [ -z "$holder" ] && ! pgrep -f 'lake build AlgebraicJacobian' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
125	       && [ $(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) )) -gt 900 ]; then
126	      echo "STALE: no live build, lock >15min old — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
127	    fi
128	  fi
129	  sleep 10
130	done
131	echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null      # record holder so a later reaper can prove liveness via kill -0
132	# … lake build … ; rm -rf "$LOCK"      # release (rm -rf, not rmdir — the pidfile makes the dir non-empty)
133	```
134	
135	Two stale shapes, both now handled above (do NOT just `sleep` forever on either):
136	- A plain FILE at the lock path is by definition stale (mkdir makes directories) — reap immediately.
137	- An orphaned DIRECTORY from a build that crashed before `rm -rf` (the 2026-07-19 C4 incident,
138	  I-0257): the OLD acquire loop only checked for a file, so it spun forever on this. Writing
139	  `$$` into `$LOCK/pid` on acquire lets the next lane prove the holder is dead (`kill -0`) and reap
140	  safely; the no-pidfile branch (a holder from before this fix) falls back to "no live build + >15min".
141	  Never reap a directory whose pidfile names a LIVE pid — that is a real build in progress.
142	
143	## 3. /tmp quota with >3 lanes
144	
145	uid-1001 tmpfs quota exhaustion (EDQUOT) bricked every Bash call machine-wide
146	(~19:00–19:20). With more than ~3 concurrent lanes, keep scratch artifacts small, clean up
147	build temp dirs, and if Bash starts failing with quota errors, stop and report rather than
148	retry-looping.
149	
150	## 4. The root import file: commit only your own lines (I-0153)
151	
152	`AlgebraicJacobian.lean` is edited by every lane. Committing the WHOLE file via any recipe
153	sweeps siblings' uncommitted import lines into HEAD — the root then references files not yet
154	in HEAD (red for fresh checkouts), and a later sibling's whole-file commit can sweep or drop
155	YOUR line the same way. Before committing the root file: run
156	`git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD -- <project>/AlgebraicJacobian.lean` — if lines
157	other than yours differ, either (a) verify every swept import's file is already committed in
158	HEAD and say so in the commit message, or (b) construct the commit from HEAD's version plus
159	only your lines (apply a minimal patch to a temp checkout of the HEAD blob). Never commit a
160	root file that references uncommitted files without naming that in the message.
161	
162	### 4a. A MINUS line in that diff is never yours (2026-07-28, run 0072)
163	
164	The check above works. The failure mode is **misreading** it, and it happened again on
165	2026-07-28: the diff printed a `-import`/`+import` pair from a sibling lane's *uncommitted*
166	worktree edit, the committing lane read it as background noise, and the commit published the
167	sibling's replacement — dropping `Picard/DivRepAffPullIndep.lean` from the import closure.
168	The file stayed in HEAD and still compiled, but was reachable from nothing: **un-rooted**,
169	i.e. I-0153 again, from a lane that had run the I-0153 check.
170	
171	So state the rule in a form that needs no judgement:
172	
173	> **A `-import` line in that diff is never yours.** The only clean result is `+import <your
174	> file>` and nothing else. Any minus line means you are about to delete another lane's root
175	> entry — stop and explain it before committing. An unexplained `+import` you did not write
176	> is the same signal: a sibling's uncommitted edit is in your worktree copy, and a minus line
177	> usually accompanies it.
178	
179	This is strictly stronger than "commit only your own lines", because you can intend that and
180	still sweep — staging the whole file is what publishes their edit, and the diff is your only
181	warning.
182	
183	**Repair additively, never by reverting.** Restore the dropped import while **keeping** the
184	other lane's new one, then verify with a full root build (the 2026-07-28 repair: 9139 jobs,
185	exit 0, with the un-rooted file rebuilt). Reverting to your own earlier root blob discards
186	their work and turns one incident into two.
187	
188	## 5. The AJCR mutex is for AJCR lake invocations only
189	
190	No cross-workspace use (an OpenGA-Horizon agent squatted it ~25 min for its own
191	`lake cache get`, silently serializing AJCR lanes against unrelated work). Other
192	workspaces must use their own lock paths.
193	
194	### 5a. Read it as per-PROJECT, not per-workspace (2026-07-28, run 0072)
195	
196	The rule above says "cross-workspace", and that wording has a hole: **AJC and AJCR are two
197	projects in the SAME workspace.** Observed live on 2026-07-28 — the AJCR mutex was held for
198	over ten minutes while the only live `lake build` belonged to an `ajc-*` lane building

201	
202	The lock path is `ajcr-locks`, so read the rule as: **only lanes building
203	`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` may take it.** AJC lanes need their own path
204	(`/tmp/claude-1001/ajc-locks/lake.lock`). Note the AJC task prompts do not mention a mutex
205	at all, which is very likely why an AJC lane reached for this one.
206	
207	### 5b. Write the pidfile — the no-pidfile fallback cannot distinguish squatter from orphan
208	
209	§2's acquire recipe writes `$$` into `$LOCK/pid` so a later lane can prove death via
210	`kill -0`. In the incident above the lock directory had **no pidfile**, so that branch could
211	not fire and the fallback ("no live `lake build AlgebraicJacobian` **and** dir >15 min old")
212	also could not fire — there *was* a live build, just not an AJCR one. Net effect: a
213	provably-non-AJCR holder is unreapable for 15 minutes.
214	
215	Two consequences for a blocked lane, both applied in that incident:
216	
217	* **Do not reap a directory whose holder you cannot prove dead**, even when you suspect a
218	  squatter. Reaping mid-build is worse than waiting.
219	* **Fall back to the narrowest check instead of blocking.** `lake env lean <file>` on the
220	  single changed file writes no shared build state and needs no lock; it is a faithful
221	  kernel check for that file. Record in the report that the mutex was unavailable and which
222	  check you substituted.

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtCoverBridge
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.OverSigmaExtension
import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Representability

/-!
# The big-site Zariski sheaf `pic⁰` and the 01JJ seam (DAT-6, stage 3)

The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an
honest sheaf for the big Zariski topology on `Scheme`, and mathlib's 01JJ
local-representability engine applied to it descends to a representation of the
degree-zero Picard functor itself on the slice.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0TypeFunctor C`: the degree-zero Picard functor with values in
  types — the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once
  (`pic0TypeFunctor_obj`/`pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply` are `rfl`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor C : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`: the Σ-extension
  `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)` — the big-site carrier.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` / **`pic0SigmaSheaf C`**: the sheaf
  certificate.  By mathlib's own reduction the big-site sheaf condition collapses to
  elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers
  (`Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange`,
  `exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology`, `Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff` — the
  `BigZariski` TODO is never touched): the Σ-components glue by
  `Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`, the fibre components glue by the DAT-6 stage-1
  evaluation bridge (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`), and the two layers are
  stitched by the stage-2 amalgamation seam (`sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff`) and
  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: **the DAT-glue seam** — given a
  chart family of relatively representable open immersions into `pic0SigmaSheaf`
  (DAT-C) that is jointly locally surjective (DAT-B), mathlib's
  `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` produces a representation of the
  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it
  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
  Σ-component of the universal element.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

/-! ## The type-valued degree-zero Picard functor -/

/-- The degree-zero Picard functor with values in types: the `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once for the Σ-extension statements. -/
noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat

@[simp]
lemma pic0TypeFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
    (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj T = pic0Subgroup C T.unop :=
  rfl

lemma pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
  rfl

/-! ## The Σ-extension as a presheaf on the big site -/

/-- **The big-site carrier of the slice trick**: the Σ-extension of the type-valued
degree-zero Picard functor, `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)`.  Reducible so
that the stage-2 `sigmaExtension` calculus applies syntactically. -/
noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaFunctor : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)

variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]

set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
-- The amalgamation seams unify the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`
-- against the Σ-extension calculus by unfolding; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap 1600000
-- precedent.
/-- **The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate of the Σ-extension** (DAT-6 keystone,
worksheet §1.2 site gap 1): mathlib's reduction collapses the sheaf condition to
elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
bridge. -/
theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
  intro Y S hS
  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
  intro x hx
  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
    congrArg Sigma.fst
      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
        pullback.condition)
  obtain ⟨aY, ha⟩ : ∃ aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k), ∀ i, 𝓤.f i ≫ aY = (x i).1 :=
    ⟨𝓤.glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair,
      fun i => 𝓤.ι_glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair i⟩
  -- the induced slice cover of `Over.mk aY` and its member sections
  haveI hop : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion
      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left :=
    fun i => 𝓤.map_prop i
  have hcov : ∀ p : (Over.mk aY).left, ∃ i, p ∈ Scheme.Hom.opensRange
      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
    intro p
    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
  -- the fibre components are a compatible family on the slice cover
  have hcompat : ∀ (i j : 𝓤.I₀) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),
      gi ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)
          = gj ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f j) (ha j) : Over.mk ((x j).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY) →
      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
    intro i j Z gi gj hg
    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat
  refine ⟨⟨aY, s⟩, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
    exact hs i
  · -- uniqueness: Σ-components by `hom_ext`, fibres by bridge separation
    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'
    obtain rfl : aY = a' := 𝓤.hom_ext aY a' fun i =>
      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)
    have hmem := (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s' ((x i).2)).mp
      (ht' i)
    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hmem

/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
consumes. -/
noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩

/-! ## The DAT-glue seam -/

/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice

end AlgebraicGeometry

29	   `V`, and this is a *composition* of presheaf morphisms.  Landed here, sorry-free.
30	2. **certify the restricted map an open immersion of presheaves** — the honest content.
31	   `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` (mathlib `MorphismProperty.relative`) has two clauses:
32	   relative representability, and the open-immersion property of every represented pullback.
33	   Step 1 supplies the *left* factor of both clauses for free
34	   (`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map_of_isOpenImmersion` +
35	   `MorphismProperty.relative_isStableUnderComposition`), so what remains is exactly the
36	   corresponding statement for `abelSigmaChart` restricted to `V = chartLocus`, i.e.
37	   CHART-U(c): on the chart locus the Abel map is a bijection onto its image because the
38	   normalized effective representative is unique there (DAT-C GAP-2).

41	*chart-locus* half is CHART-U(c) and is stated but not proved (it needs GAP-2 plus the
42	classifier, and the openness of the locus itself, `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`).

46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map` — an open immersion of schemes is
47	  an open immersion of presheaves under yoneda.  This is mathlib's `relative_map` at

49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.restrictChart` — the chart map restricted to an open of the source.
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` — **the composition half of

52	  restriction of it along an open immersion.  Unconditional in the restriction.

75	/-! ## An open immersion of schemes is one of presheaves -/
76	
77	/-- **Open immersions transfer through yoneda**: for an open immersion of schemes
78	`g : X ⟶ Y`, the induced map of yoneda presheaves satisfies `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`.

80	This is mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative_map` specialised to `F := yoneda` and
81	`P := @IsOpenImmersion`; the two side conditions it needs — that open immersions are stable
82	under base change, and that yoneda preserves the relevant pullbacks (it is fully faithful and
83	`Scheme` has pullbacks) — are discharged by instances.

85	Recorded as a named lemma because it is the *only* source of `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`
86	facts anywhere in this tree that does not go through a chart certificate: every restriction
87	of a chart map is built from it. -/
88	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y)
89	    [IsOpenImmersion g] :
90	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (yoneda.map g) :=
91	  MorphismProperty.relative_map (P := @IsOpenImmersion) (F := yoneda) ‹IsOpenImmersion g›
92

95	/-- **The chart map restricted to an open of its source.**
96	
97	`f` is the unrestricted chart map (in practice `abelSigmaChart`, whose source is the divisor
98	scheme) and `V` an open subscheme of the source; the restriction is the composition with the
99	yoneda image of the open inclusion.

102	presheaves — see the `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep` header — while its restriction to the locus where
103	the fibre is a single point is.  This definition is neutral about which open `V` is; the
104	chart-locus choice enters only in the certificate. -/
105	def restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
106	    (V : X.Opens) : yoneda.obj (V : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
107	  yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f

110	presheaves along an open immersion is again one.

112	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is `MorphismProperty.relative` at `yoneda`, which is stable under
113	composition (`MorphismProperty.relative_isStableUnderComposition`, needing `yoneda` full and
114	faithful and `IsOpenImmersion` stable under composition — all instances).  Together with
115	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map` this discharges, for free and in full generality, the
116	part of C9b that is bookkeeping.

119	hypothesis `hfV`.  For `f := abelSigmaChart` that hypothesis is FALSE for `V = ⊤` and is

121	uniqueness of the normalized effective representative (DAT-C GAP-2) and the classifier.  A

    [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L] (j : E.Carrier →ₐ[K] L) :
    PicEtAff.degAff K (PicEtAff.mk C E x)
      = relPicDeg L (relPicAlgMap C (j.restrictScalars k)
          (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier))) :=
  relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap_congr x.2 (degAffHom E) j

/-- **The anchor of the plus-class degree on field covers**: on a class represented by
a descent class `y` on the field cover `ofField L`, the degree is the relative degree
over `L` of `y` transported through the carrier identification `ofFieldEquiv`. -/
theorem PicEtAff.degAff_mk_ofField (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L]
    [IsScalarTower k K L] [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]
    (y : descentClasses C (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L)) :
    PicEtAff.degAff K (PicEtAff.mk C (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L) y)
      = relPicDeg L (relPicAlgMap C
          ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).toAlgHom.restrictScalars k)
          (y : relPic C (overSpec k (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L).Carrier))) :=
  PicEtAff.degAff_mk _ y L (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).toAlgHom

end RepField

/-! ## Normalizations: unit and additivity -/

section Calculus

variable {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]

/-- The degree of the trivial plus class is zero. -/
@[simp]
theorem PicEtAff.degAff_one : PicEtAff.degAff K (1 : PicEtAff C K) = 0 := by
  rw [PicEtAff.one_def,
    PicEtAff.degAff_mk (.self K) 1 K (Algebra.EtaleCover.selfEquiv K).toAlgHom,
    show ((1 : descentClasses C (.self K))
        : relPic C (overSpec k (Algebra.EtaleCover.self K).Carrier)) = 1 from rfl,
    map_one, relPicDeg_one]

/-- **The unit normalization of the plus-class degree** (needed by G-D8's degree
certificates): on a class pulled back from the base along the unit of the plus
construction, the degree is the relative degree over the base field itself — the
trivial cover is refined by the field cover of `K` itself. -/
theorem PicEtAff.degAff_unit (z : relPic C (overSpec k K)) :
    PicEtAff.degAff K (PicEtAff.unit C K z) = relPicDeg K z := by
  have hrep : PicEtAff.unit C K z
      = PicEtAff.mk C (.self K)
          ⟨relPicAlgMap C
              ((Algebra.ofId K (Algebra.EtaleCover.self K).Carrier).restrictScalars k) z,
            PicEtAff.tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self K) z⟩ := rfl
  rw [hrep,
    PicEtAff.degAff_mk (.self K) _ K (Algebra.EtaleCover.selfEquiv K).toAlgHom,
    ← relPicAlgMap_comp,
    show ((Algebra.EtaleCover.selfEquiv K).toAlgHom.restrictScalars k).comp
        ((Algebra.ofId K (Algebra.EtaleCover.self K).Carrier).restrictScalars k)
      = AlgHom.id k K from AlgHom.ext fun r => by
        simp [Algebra.ofId_apply],
    relPicAlgMap_id]

/-- **Additivity of the plus-class degree**: the degree of a product of plus classes is
the sum of the degrees.  Represent the product on the product cover (`mk_mul_mk`),
refine to a single finite separable field, and read all three degrees there —
`relPicDeg` is a homomorphism. -/
theorem PicEtAff.degAff_mul (a b : PicEtAff C K) :
    PicEtAff.degAff K (a * b) = PicEtAff.degAff K a + PicEtAff.degAff K b := by
  induction a using PicEtAff.ind with | _ E x =>
  induction b using PicEtAff.ind with | _ F y =>
  obtain ⟨L, _, _, _, _, ⟨ℓ⟩⟩ := (E.prod F).exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom
  letI : Algebra k L := ((algebraMap K L).comp (algebraMap k K)).toAlgebra
  haveI : IsScalarTower k K L := .of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
  rw [PicEtAff.mk_mul_mk, PicEtAff.degAff_mk (E.prod F) _ L ℓ,
    PicEtAff.degAff_mk E x L (ℓ.comp (E.prodInl F)),
    PicEtAff.degAff_mk F y L (ℓ.comp (E.prodInr F)),
    show ((descentMap C (E.prodInl F) x * descentMap C (E.prodInr F) y :
          descentClasses C (E.prod F))
        : relPic C (overSpec k (E.prod F).Carrier))
      = relPicAlgMap C ((E.prodInl F).restrictScalars k)
          (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier))
        * relPicAlgMap C ((E.prodInr F).restrictScalars k)
          (y : relPic C (overSpec k F.Carrier)) from rfl,
    map_mul, relPicDeg_mul,
    show (ℓ.comp (E.prodInl F)).restrictScalars k
      = (ℓ.restrictScalars k).comp ((E.prodInl F).restrictScalars k) from rfl,
    show (ℓ.comp (E.prodInr F)).restrictScalars k
      = (ℓ.restrictScalars k).comp ((E.prodInr F).restrictScalars k) from rfl,
    relPicAlgMap_comp, relPicAlgMap_comp]

/-- The degree of an inverse plus class is the negation of the degree. -/
theorem PicEtAff.degAff_inv (a : PicEtAff C K) :
    PicEtAff.degAff K a⁻¹ = -PicEtAff.degAff K a := by
  have h := PicEtAff.degAff_mul a⁻¹ a
  rw [inv_mul_cancel, PicEtAff.degAff_one] at h
  omega

end Calculus

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

extension `A → A'` restricts a plus class by base-changing its representing cover
(`Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChange`) and transporting the descent datum along the canonical
inclusion of the carrier into its base change.  Following the mathlib idiom for maps along
base extensions, the extension is carried as instances `[Algebra A A'] [IsScalarTower k A A']`
rather than as an explicit `k`-algebra map.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentBaseChange C A' E`: transport of descent classes along the base
  change of the cover — well-posed because the two coprojections of the base-changed double
  cover restrict to `A`-algebra maps out of the original carrier, so the keystone
  `relPicAlgMap_congr` applies.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map C A'`: the induced restriction homomorphism
  `PicEtAff C A →* PicEtAff C A'`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_unit`: naturality of the unit of the plus construction.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_id`, `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_map`: the functor
  laws — both are instances of `relPicAlgMap_congr`, which erases the difference between
  any two transports out of the same descent class.

Together with the unit (`PicEtAff.unit`), this is the presheaf structure of the one-step
étale plus of the relative Picard functor on affine tests; the comparison theorems
(separatedness, rigidification under a section) consume this interface.
-/

universe u

/-! ## The restriction homomorphism -/

private def mapSig (p : Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E) :
    Σ E' : Algebra.EtaleCover A', descentClasses C E' :=
  ⟨p.1.baseChange A', descentBaseChange C A' p.1 p.2⟩

/- Stated with the sigma pairs fully destructured, so that no goal ever mentions a
sigma-literal projection. -/
private lemma mapSig_rel {E F' : Algebra.EtaleCover A} {x : descentClasses C E}
    {y : descentClasses C F'} (F : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
    (g : F'.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) (hfg : descentMap C f x = descentMap C g y) :
    ∃ (G : Algebra.EtaleCover A')
      (f' : (E.baseChange A').Carrier →ₐ[A'] G.Carrier)
      (g' : (F'.baseChange A').Carrier →ₐ[A'] G.Carrier),
      descentMap C f' (descentBaseChange C A' E x)
        = descentMap C g' (descentBaseChange C A' F' y) :=
  ⟨F.baseChange A', Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChangeMap A' f,
    Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChangeMap A' g, by
      rw [descentMap_baseChangeMap, descentMap_baseChangeMap, hfg]⟩

private lemma mapSig_compat {p q : Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E}
    (h : p ≈ q) : mapSig C A' p ≈ mapSig C A' q := by
  obtain ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩ := h
  exact mapSig_rel C A' F f g hfg

private def mapFun : PicEtAff C A → PicEtAff C A' :=
  Quotient.map (mapSig C A') fun _ _ h => mapSig_compat C A' h

private lemma mapFun_mk (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E) :
    mapFun C A' (mk C E x) = mk C (E.baseChange A') (descentBaseChange C A' E x) :=
  rfl

private lemma mapFun_mul (a b : PicEtAff C A) :
    mapFun C A' (a * b) = mapFun C A' a * mapFun C A' b := by
  induction a using ind with | _ E x =>
  induction b using ind with | _ F y =>
  have h₁ : mapFun C A' (mk C E x)
      = mk C ((E.prod F).baseChange A')
          (descentBaseChange C A' (E.prod F) (descentMap C (E.prodInl F) x)) := by
    rw [← mk_descentMap C (E.prodInl F) x, mapFun_mk]
  have h₂ : mapFun C A' (mk C F y)
      = mk C ((E.prod F).baseChange A')
          (descentBaseChange C A' (E.prod F) (descentMap C (E.prodInr F) y)) := by
    rw [← mk_descentMap C (E.prodInr F) y, mapFun_mk]
  rw [mk_mul_mk, mapFun_mk, map_mul, ← mk_mul_mk_same, h₁, h₂]

/-- Restriction of étale-plus Picard classes along a base extension `A → A'` of affine
tests: base-change the representing cover and transport the descent datum along the
canonical inclusion of the carrier into its base change. -/
def map : PicEtAff C A →* PicEtAff C A' :=
  MonoidHom.mk' (mapFun C A') (mapFun_mul C A')

@[simp]
lemma map_mk (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E) :
    map C A' (mk C E x) = mk C (E.baseChange A') (descentBaseChange C A' E x) :=
  rfl

/-! ## Naturality of the unit and the functor laws -/

/-- The unit of the plus construction is natural in the test algebra. -/
theorem map_unit (x : relPic C (overSpec k A)) :
    map C A' (unit C A x)
      = unit C A' (relPicAlgMap C (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A A') x) := by
  have hj : (((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChangeInclude A').restrictScalars k).comp
        ((Algebra.ofId A (Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).Carrier).restrictScalars k)
      = ((((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChange A').fromSelf).restrictScalars k).comp
          (((Algebra.ofId A' (Algebra.EtaleCover.self A').Carrier).restrictScalars k).comp
            (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A A')) := by
    ext a
    simp only [AlgHom.coe_comp, AlgHom.coe_restrictScalars', Function.comp_apply,
      Algebra.ofId_apply, IsScalarTower.coe_toAlgHom', AlgHom.commutes]
    exact IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply A A' _ a
  have hval : relPicAlgMap C
        (((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChangeInclude A').restrictScalars k)
        (relPicAlgMap C
          ((Algebra.ofId A (Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).Carrier).restrictScalars k) x)
      = relPicAlgMap C
          ((((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChange A').fromSelf).restrictScalars k)
          (relPicAlgMap C
            ((Algebra.ofId A' (Algebra.EtaleCover.self A').Carrier).restrictScalars k)
            (relPicAlgMap C (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A A') x)) := by
    rw [← relPicAlgMap_comp, ← relPicAlgMap_comp, ← relPicAlgMap_comp, hj,
      AlgHom.comp_assoc]
  calc map C A' (unit C A x)
      = mk C ((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChange A')
          (descentMap C ((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChange A').fromSelf
            ⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (Algebra.EtaleCover.self A')
              (relPicAlgMap C (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A A') x)⟩) :=
        congrArg (mk C ((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChange A')) (Subtype.ext hval)
    _ = mk C (Algebra.EtaleCover.self A')
          ⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (Algebra.EtaleCover.self A')
            (relPicAlgMap C (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A A') x)⟩ :=
        mk_descentMap C ((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChange A').fromSelf _
    _ = unit C A' (relPicAlgMap C (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A A') x) := rfl

/-- Restriction along the trivial base extension is the identity. -/
theorem map_id (a : PicEtAff C A) : map C A a = a := by
  induction a using ind with | _ E x =>

/-!
# θ: the base-field comparison of the degree-zero Picard functor (Wave 7, W7-B4b)

For a field embedding `k → L` and the curve bundle `C` over `k` with base change
`C_L = (baseChange k L).obj C`, the componentwise lift of the B-2 shuffle
(`Picard/PicEtCrossBase.lean`) restricts to the degree-zero subfunctors and assembles
into the natural isomorphism θ of the ratified D2-i shape,
`θ : Pic⁰_{C_L/L} ≅ (Over.map σ)ᵒᵖ ⋙ Pic⁰_{C/k}` in `CommGrpCat`-valued functors
(`σ = Spec.map (algebraMap k L)`).

* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAff_baseFieldShuffle`: **degree invariance of the B-2 shuffle at
  a field test** — `degAff K (baseFieldShuffle x) = degAff K x` for `K` in the tower
  `k → L → K`.  Both sides are read by `degAff_mk` on a common finite separable
  refinement `M/K` of the representing cover; the readings match through the
  `relPicAlgMap` square `relPicCrossBase_relPicAlgMap` and B-4a's degree seam
  `relPicDeg_relPicCrossBase` at `M` (the deg-d5b D1 discipline: the only licensed
  cross-presentation degree route).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_pushFieldPoint_picEtCrossBase`: **the `degAt` matching** —
  the degree of a class on the pushed test at a pushed field point equals the degree of
  its lift at the field point itself, by naturality of the lift, the affine face, and
  the shuffle degree invariance.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_pic0Subgroup_picEtCrossBase_iff`: **the degree-zero
  restriction** — a class and its lift are simultaneously degree-zero, by B-4a's engine
  `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff_of_degAt_pushFieldPoint_eq` fed with the `degAt` matching.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0CrossBaseEquiv`: the induced isomorphism of degree-zero
  subgroups `pic⁰(C_L, T) ≃* pic⁰(C, (Over.map σ).obj T)`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Theta`: **θ** (Wave-7 brick B-4b, worksheet §D2 W7-B4b row) —
  the `CommGrpCat`-valued natural isomorphism
  `pic0Functor C_L ≅ (Over.map σ).op ⋙ pic0Functor C`, with `rfl`-grade component
  anchors `pic0Theta_hom_app_coe`/`pic0Theta_inv_app_coe`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0ThetaType`: the Type-valued form, by whiskering with
  `forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat ⋙ forget GrpCat` against `pic0TypeFunctor` (the D2-i
  massage; consumed by B-5's `RepresentableBy.ofIso` transport).

finiteness, separability or Galois content — so composed shuffles at towers
`k → L → M` are legal inputs for the K-1 θ-cocycle.

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
variable (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

/-! ## Degree invariance of the shuffle at a field test -/

/-- **Degree invariance of the base-field shuffle at a field test** (the B-4b degree
keystone): for a field `K` in the tower `k → L → K`, the B-2 shuffle preserves the
plus-class degree.  Both sides are read by `degAff_mk` on a common finite separable
refinement `M/K` of the representing cover; the readings match through the
`relPicAlgMap` square and B-4a's degree seam `relPicDeg_relPicCrossBase` at `M`. -/
theorem degAff_baseFieldShuffle (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Algebra L K]
    [IsScalarTower k L K] (x : PicEtAff C K) :
    PicEtAff.degAff K (PicEtAff.baseFieldShuffle k L C K x) = PicEtAff.degAff K x := by
  induction x using PicEtAff.ind with
  | mk E y =>
    obtain ⟨M, _, _, _, _, ⟨j⟩⟩ := E.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom
    letI : Algebra L M := ((algebraMap K M).comp (algebraMap L K)).toAlgebra
    haveI : IsScalarTower L K M := .of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
    letI : Algebra k M := ((algebraMap L M).comp (algebraMap k L)).toAlgebra
    haveI : IsScalarTower k L M := .of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
    haveI : IsScalarTower k K M := .of_algebraMap_eq fun r => by
      rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply k L K r]; rfl
    rw [PicEtAff.baseFieldShuffle_mk,
      PicEtAff.degAff_mk E ((crossBaseTransportFamily k L C).descentHom E y) M j,
      PicEtAff.degAff_mk E y M j,
      PicEtAff.crossBaseTransportFamily_descentHom_coe,
      ← relPicCrossBase_relPicAlgMap k L C E.Carrier M (j.restrictScalars L),
      relPicDeg_relPicCrossBase]
    rfl

/-! ## The `degAt` matching at pushed field points -/

section DegAtMatching

variable {T : Over (Spec (.of L))}

/-- **The `degAt` matching at pushed field points**: the degree of an étale Picard class
of `C` on the pushed test `(Over.map σ).obj T` at a pushed field point is the degree of
its componentwise lift at the field point itself.  Naturality of the lift moves the
restriction to the affine test `overSpec L K`, the affine face identifies the lift with
the B-2 shuffle there, and the shuffle preserves the degree. -/
theorem degAt_pushFieldPoint_picEtCrossBase
    (s : picEt C ((Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).obj T))
    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Algebra L K] [IsScalarTower k L K]
    (t : overSpec L K ⟶ T) :
    degAt s (pushFieldPoint k t) = degAt (picEtCrossBase k L C T s) t :=
  calc degAt s (pushFieldPoint k t)
      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K
          (picEtMap C (mapOverSpecIso k L K).inv
            (picEtMap C
              ((Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).map t) s))) :=
        congrArg (fun z => PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K z))
          (picEtMap_comp C
            ((Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).map t)
            (mapOverSpecIso k L K).inv s)
    _ = PicEtAff.degAff K (PicEtAff.baseFieldShuffle k L C K
          (picEtAffineEquiv C K
            (picEtMap C (mapOverSpecIso k L K).inv
              (picEtMap C
                ((Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).map t)
                s)))) :=
        (degAff_baseFieldShuffle k L C K _).symm
    _ = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv ((baseChange k L).obj C) K
          (picEtCrossBase k L C (overSpec L K)
            (picEtMap C
              ((Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).map t) s))) :=
        congrArg (PicEtAff.degAff K)
          (picEtAffineEquiv_picEtCrossBase k L C K _).symm
    _ = degAt (picEtCrossBase k L C T s) t :=
        (congrArg (fun z => PicEtAff.degAff K
            (picEtAffineEquiv ((baseChange k L).obj C) K z))
          (picEtMap_picEtCrossBase k L C t s)).symm

/-! ## `classDeg` kills the classes from the base -/

/-- **The degree vanishes on classes pulled back from the base field**: `Spec K` is a
one-point space, so its Čech Picard group is trivial and every class of `picFromBase` is
trivial. -/
theorem classDeg_eq_zero_of_mem_picFromBase {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    {L : (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic} (hL : L ∈ picFromBase C (overSpec k K)) :
    classDeg K L = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨N, rfl⟩ := (mem_picFromBase_iff C).mp hL
  haveI : Subsingleton (overSpec k K).left :=
    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum K))
  rw [Scheme.CechPic.eq_one_of_subsingleton (overSpec k K).left N, map_one, classDeg_one]

/-! ## The relative degree -/

/-- **The degree on the relative Picard group over a field** (worksheet SB-5, first descent
gadget): `classDeg K` descends along `relPicMk` to the quotient
`relPic C (overSpec k K) = CechPic(C_K) ⧸ picFromBase`, because the Čech Picard group of the
one-point scheme `Spec K` is trivial.  The `degAt` brick (SB-6) reads the degree of a
field-representative of an étale-locally-trivial class through this homomorphism. -/
noncomputable def relPicDeg (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
    Additive (relPic C (overSpec k K)) →+ ℤ :=
  MonoidHom.toAdditiveLeft
    (QuotientGroup.lift (picFromBase C (overSpec k K))
      (AddMonoidHom.toMultiplicativeRight (classDeg K))
      (fun L hL => by
        have h0 : classDeg K L = 0 := classDeg_eq_zero_of_mem_picFromBase hL
        rw [MonoidHom.mem_ker]
        change Multiplicative.ofAdd (classDeg K L) = 1
        rw [h0, ofAdd_zero]))

/-- **The anchor of the relative degree**: on the class of `L`, the relative degree is
`classDeg K L`. -/
@[simp]
theorem relPicDeg_relPicMk (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (L : (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic) :
    relPicDeg K (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) L) = classDeg K L :=
  rfl

/-- **E-iv-alg descended to the relative Picard group** (worksheet SB-5, second descent
gadget): the relative degree is invariant under restriction along `Spec` of a `k`-algebra
map `φ : K₁ →ₐ[k] K₂` of field extensions — the degree of a relative Picard class does not
depend on the field over which it is presented. -/
theorem relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap {K₁ K₂ : Type u} [Field K₁] [Algebra k K₁] [Field K₂]
    [Algebra k K₂] (φ : K₁ →ₐ[k] K₂) (x : relPic C (overSpec k K₁)) :
    relPicDeg K₂ (relPicAlgMap C φ x) = relPicDeg K₁ x := by
  induction x using relPic.ind with
  | mk L =>
    have h1 : relPicAlgMap C φ (relPicMk C (overSpec k K₁) L)
        = relPicMk C (overSpec k K₂)
          (Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left) L) :=
      relPicMap_mk C (Over.overSpecMap φ) L
    rw [h1, relPicDeg_relPicMk, relPicDeg_relPicMk,
      classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition C φ L]

end AlgebraicGeometry

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtAff
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.RelPicDegree

/-!
# The degree on the étale plus construction (gap G-D6, worksheet SB-6)

For the challenge curve `C` over `k` and a field extension `K` of `k`, a class of the
étale plus construction `PicEtAff C K` is represented by a descent class on an étale
cover of `Spec K`, and every cover is refined by a single finite separable field
extension `L/K` (cofinality, `Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`).
On a field representative the relative degree `relPicDeg L` (SB-5) reads an honest
integer, and the **zigzag (WD)** shows this value does not depend on any choice.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap_congr` — leg (i) of the zigzag: a descent
  class read through any two `K`-algebra maps into finite separable field extensions
  has one degree.  The two readings are compared inside a field refinement of the
  product of the two field covers; the transport choice is immaterial by the landed
  keystone `relPicAlgMap_congr`, and the value along each leg is invariant by
  `relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap` (E-iv-alg descended).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicDeg_eq_of_descentMap_eq` — **the zigzag (WD)**: field
  readings of two descent-class representatives identified after transport to a common
  refinement agree.  No Galois theory appears: Galois twisting of the transport is a
  special case of `relPicAlgMap_congr`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.degAff K : PicEtAff C K → ℤ` — the degree of an
  étale-locally trivial relative Picard class, by `Quotient.lift` of the reading
  through a *chosen* field refinement, with (WD) as the compatibility proof.
  `Classical.choice` only ever picks representatives; the value is pinned by the
  equality lemma `degAff_mk`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.degAff_mk` — **the master equality**: on `mk C E x` the
  degree is the reading of `x` through *any* `K`-algebra map of the cover carrier into
  a finite separable field extension.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.degAff_mk_ofField` — the anchor on field covers:
  `degAff (mk C (ofField L) y)` is `relPicDeg L` of `y` transported through the carrier
  identification `ofFieldEquiv`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.degAff_one`/`degAff_mul`/`degAff_inv` — additivity.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.degAff_unit` — the unit normalization
  `degAff (unit C K z) = relPicDeg K z`, consumed by G-D8's degree certificates.

The `degAt`/`pic0Functor` endpoints (SB-7) consuming this interface live in
`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0Functor`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-! ## The `relPicDeg` calculus -/

/-- The relative degree of a product of relative Picard classes is the sum of the
degrees (`relPicDeg` is a homomorphism from the multiplicative relative Picard group,
stated on the multiplicative product for direct use). -/
theorem relPicDeg_mul (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (x y : relPic C (overSpec k K)) :
    relPicDeg K (x * y) = relPicDeg K x + relPicDeg K y :=
  (relPicDeg K).map_add x y

/-- The relative degree of the trivial class is zero. -/
@[simp]
theorem relPicDeg_one (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
    relPicDeg K (1 : relPic C (overSpec k K)) = 0 :=
  (relPicDeg K).map_zero

/-! ## The zigzag (WD) -/

section Zigzag

variable {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]

/-- **Leg (i) of the zigzag (WD)**: a descent class on an étale cover of `Spec K`, read
through any two `K`-algebra maps of the cover carrier into finite separable field
extensions of `K`, has one relative degree.  The two readings are compared inside a
finite separable field refinement of the product of the two field covers: the transport
choice is immaterial by the descent keystone `relPicAlgMap_congr`, and the value along
each comparison leg is invariant by `relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap` (E-iv-alg descended). -/
theorem relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap_congr {E : Algebra.EtaleCover K}
    {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)} (hx : x ∈ descentClasses C E)
    {L₁ : Type u} [Field L₁] [Algebra k L₁] [Algebra K L₁] [IsScalarTower k K L₁]
    [Module.Finite K L₁] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L₁]
    {L₂ : Type u} [Field L₂] [Algebra k L₂] [Algebra K L₂] [IsScalarTower k K L₂]
    [Module.Finite K L₂] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L₂]
    (j₁ : E.Carrier →ₐ[K] L₁) (j₂ : E.Carrier →ₐ[K] L₂) :
    relPicDeg L₁ (relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x)
      = relPicDeg L₂ (relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x) := by
  obtain ⟨M, _, _, _, _, ⟨ℓ⟩⟩ :=
    ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L₁).prod
      (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L₂)).exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom
  letI : Algebra k M := ((algebraMap K M).comp (algebraMap k K)).toAlgebra
  haveI : IsScalarTower k K M := .of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
  set θ₁ : L₁ →ₐ[K] M :=
    (ℓ.comp ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L₁).prodInl
        (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L₂))).comp
      (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L₁).symm.toAlgHom with hθ₁
  set θ₂ : L₂ →ₐ[K] M :=
    (ℓ.comp ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L₁).prodInr
        (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L₂))).comp
      (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L₂).symm.toAlgHom with hθ₂
  calc relPicDeg L₁ (relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x)
      = relPicDeg M (relPicAlgMap C (θ₁.restrictScalars k)
          (relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x)) :=
        (relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap (θ₁.restrictScalars k) _).symm
    _ = relPicDeg M (relPicAlgMap C ((θ₁.comp j₁).restrictScalars k) x) := by
        rw [show (θ₁.comp j₁).restrictScalars k
            = (θ₁.restrictScalars k).comp (j₁.restrictScalars k) from rfl,
          relPicAlgMap_comp]
    _ = relPicDeg M (relPicAlgMap C ((θ₂.comp j₂).restrictScalars k) x) := by
        rw [relPicAlgMap_congr C (θ₁.comp j₁) (θ₂.comp j₂) hx]
    _ = relPicDeg M (relPicAlgMap C (θ₂.restrictScalars k)
          (relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x)) := by
        rw [show (θ₂.comp j₂).restrictScalars k
            = (θ₂.restrictScalars k).comp (j₂.restrictScalars k) from rfl,
          relPicAlgMap_comp]
    _ = relPicDeg L₂ (relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x) :=
        relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap (θ₂.restrictScalars k) _

/-- **The zigzag (WD)** — well-definedness of the plus-class degree, both axes in one
lemma: two descent-class representatives identified after transport to a common
refinement (`descentMap C f x₁ = descentMap C g x₂`, the plus-construction setoid) have
equal field readings, through *any* field refinements.  Route: refine the common cover
`G` to a single finite separable field (cofinality), compare each reading with the
reading through the refined leg by `relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap_congr`, and cross over along
the descent equality.  No Galois theory appears. -/
theorem relPicDeg_eq_of_descentMap_eq {E₁ E₂ G : Algebra.EtaleCover K}
    {x₁ : descentClasses C E₁} {x₂ : descentClasses C E₂}
    {f : E₁.Carrier →ₐ[K] G.Carrier} {g : E₂.Carrier →ₐ[K] G.Carrier}
    (hfg : descentMap C f x₁ = descentMap C g x₂)
    {L₁ : Type u} [Field L₁] [Algebra k L₁] [Algebra K L₁] [IsScalarTower k K L₁]
    [Module.Finite K L₁] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L₁]
    {L₂ : Type u} [Field L₂] [Algebra k L₂] [Algebra K L₂] [IsScalarTower k K L₂]
    [Module.Finite K L₂] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L₂]
    (j₁ : E₁.Carrier →ₐ[K] L₁) (j₂ : E₂.Carrier →ₐ[K] L₂) :
    relPicDeg L₁ (relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k)
        (x₁ : relPic C (overSpec k E₁.Carrier)))
      = relPicDeg L₂ (relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k)
          (x₂ : relPic C (overSpec k E₂.Carrier))) := by
  obtain ⟨N, _, _, _, _, ⟨ℓ⟩⟩ := G.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom
  letI : Algebra k N := ((algebraMap K N).comp (algebraMap k K)).toAlgebra
  haveI : IsScalarTower k K N := .of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
  have hcoe : relPicAlgMap C (f.restrictScalars k)
        (x₁ : relPic C (overSpec k E₁.Carrier))
      = relPicAlgMap C (g.restrictScalars k)
        (x₂ : relPic C (overSpec k E₂.Carrier)) :=
    congrArg Subtype.val hfg
  calc relPicDeg L₁ (relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k)
          (x₁ : relPic C (overSpec k E₁.Carrier)))
      = relPicDeg N (relPicAlgMap C ((ℓ.comp f).restrictScalars k)
          (x₁ : relPic C (overSpec k E₁.Carrier))) :=
        relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap_congr x₁.2 j₁ (ℓ.comp f)
    _ = relPicDeg N (relPicAlgMap C (ℓ.restrictScalars k)
          (relPicAlgMap C (f.restrictScalars k)
            (x₁ : relPic C (overSpec k E₁.Carrier)))) := by
        rw [show (ℓ.comp f).restrictScalars k
            = (ℓ.restrictScalars k).comp (f.restrictScalars k) from rfl,
          relPicAlgMap_comp]
    _ = relPicDeg N (relPicAlgMap C (ℓ.restrictScalars k)
          (relPicAlgMap C (g.restrictScalars k)
            (x₂ : relPic C (overSpec k E₂.Carrier)))) := by rw [hcoe]
    _ = relPicDeg N (relPicAlgMap C ((ℓ.comp g).restrictScalars k)
          (x₂ : relPic C (overSpec k E₂.Carrier))) := by
        rw [show (ℓ.comp g).restrictScalars k
            = (ℓ.restrictScalars k).comp (g.restrictScalars k) from rfl,
          relPicAlgMap_comp]
    _ = relPicDeg L₂ (relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k)
          (x₂ : relPic C (overSpec k E₂.Carrier))) :=
        (relPicDeg_relPicAlgMap_congr x₂.2 j₂ (ℓ.comp g)).symm

end Zigzag
